page: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU runs at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes 2835 GB of local NVMe storage and supports Premium Storage. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong multi-core performance, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 20503.0, which places it in the top 10% of tested systems. Stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores are also highly competitive, ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is high at 3648.29 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write speeds fall into the average range.

With its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D48alds_v6 represents a cost-efficient option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive RAM footprints. It performs exceptionally well in multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and small-model LLM text generation. However, the lack of a GPU and the limited 2.0 GB of RAM per core make it poorly suited for large-scale LLM text generation, as evidenced by a low 2.56 tokens/sec on 70B model text generation. The server is highly appropriate for database operations, web serving, software build pipelines, and localized data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v6 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 48 vCPUs, 96.0 GB of RAM, and 2835 GB of local storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance delivers strong performance across multi-core benchmarks, including a top-10% Geekbench multi-core score of 20503.0 and strong Passmark CPU results. While its 2.0 GB of RAM per core and lack of GPU acceleration limit its effectiveness for large-scale LLM inference, it excels in multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and database operations. This hardware profile offers a cost-efficient balance of high-frequency compute and substantial local storage, making it well-suited for build pipelines, web serving, and database workloads.
